# Whisper

[[Blog]](https://openai.com/blog/whisper)
[[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.04356)
[[Model card]](https://github.com/openai/whisper/blob/main/model-card.md)
[[Colab example]](https://colab.research.google.com/github/openai/whisper/blob/master/notebooks/LibriSpeech.ipynb)

Whisper is a general-purpose speech recognition model. It is trained on a large dataset of diverse audio and is also a multitasking model that can perform multilingual speech recognition, speech translation, and language identification.


## Approach

![Approach](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/whisper/main/approach.png)

A Transformer sequence-to-sequence model is trained on various speech processing tasks, including multilingual speech recognition, speech translation, spoken language identification, and voice activity detection. These tasks are jointly represented as a sequence of tokens to be predicted by the decoder, allowing a single model to replace many stages of a traditional speech-processing pipeline. The multitask training format uses a set of special tokens that serve as task specifiers or classification targets.


## Setup

We used Python 3.9.9 and [PyTorch](https://pytorch.org/) 1.10.1 to train and test our models, but the codebase is expected to be compatible with Python 3.8-3.11 and recent PyTorch versions. The codebase also depends on a few Python packages, most notably [OpenAI's tiktoken](https://github.com/openai/tiktoken) for their fast tokenizer implementation. You can download and install (or update to) the latest release of Whisper with the following command:

    pip install -U openai-whisper

Alternatively, the following command will pull and install the latest commit from this repository, along with its Python dependencies:

    pip install git+https://github.com/openai/whisper.git 

To update the package to the latest version of this repository, please run:

    pip install --upgrade --no-deps --force-reinstall git+https://github.com/openai/whisper.git

It also requires the command-line tool [`ffmpeg`](https://ffmpeg.org/) to be installed on your system, which is available from most package managers:

```bash
# on Ubuntu or Debian
sudo apt update && sudo apt install ffmpeg

# on Arch Linux
sudo pacman -S ffmpeg

# on MacOS using Homebrew (https://brew.sh/)
brew install ffmpeg

# on Windows using Chocolatey (https://chocolatey.org/)
choco install ffmpeg

# on Windows using Scoop (https://scoop.sh/)
scoop install ffmpeg
```

# tinglongWu — Taiwanese 聽攏有 (thiann lóng ū): "I understood it all". Real-time speech translation, offline at runtime and verifiable (install and model download need the network; the in-process guard is defence in depth, not proof, see Privacy model).

[English](README.md) | [繁體中文](README.zh-TW.md) | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

Architecture / 架構 / 架构: [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) · [zh-TW](docs/ARCHITECTURE.zh-TW.md) · [zh-CN](docs/ARCHITECTURE.zh-CN.md)

Fully local, offline, real-time speech translator: **system audio output -> capture -> ASR -> translate -> text**.
It captures whatever the PC plays (the system output mix, not per-app). There is no network use at runtime; only setup / first-run model download uses the network.
Nothing leaves your machine: no cloud APIs, no telemetry, no audio or transcripts written to disk.

```
[RU] Привет, как дела?
[EN] Hello, how are you?
[ZH] 你好，你過得怎麼樣？
```

## One-command install (Windows / Mac / Linux)

Each command installs the exact version of the latest GitHub Release (`main` is stable; `dev` is for development). Re-running is safe.

| OS | Command |
|---|---|
| Windows (PowerShell) | `irm https://github.com/sunososobro-hub/tinglongwu/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 \| iex` |
| macOS (Terminal) | `curl -fsSL https://github.com/sunososobro-hub/tinglongwu/releases/latest/download/mac_install.sh \| bash` |
| Linux (bash) | `curl -fsSL https://github.com/sunososobro-hub/tinglongwu/releases/latest/download/install.sh \| bash` |

Each release also lists `SHA256SUMS.txt`; to check a script before running it, download it and compare. The Linux installer asks y/N before any `apt` step and downloads no models (the menu asks before every download). The Windows command downloads the source to `%USERPROFILE%\tinglongwu` and runs the same `install.ps1` as below (the execution-policy bypass is for that one child process only).

## Quick install (Windows)

For Windows 10/11 with an NVIDIA GPU (works without one, just slower). You need [Python 3.12](https://www.python.org/downloads/windows/) first (tick **Add python.exe to PATH** in its installer).

1. On GitHub click **Code > Download ZIP**, then right-click the ZIP > **Extract All**.
2. Open the folder and double-click **`install.bat`**. Wait (10-30 min, up to ~10 GB download; safe to re-run if interrupted).
3. Double-click the new desktop shortcut **聽攏有 tinglongWu**.

candidates.description: Faster speech off signals for spec gen voice pipelines
candidates.readme_excerpt:
# RealtimeVAD

*Know that the speaker stopped, about 110 ms before Silero does.*

[RealtimeSTT](https://github.com/KoljaB/RealtimeSTT) · [RealtimeTTS](https://github.com/KoljaB/RealtimeTTS) · [Live demo](https://github.com/KoljaB/RealtimeVAD/blob/main/demo/README.md) · [Spec](https://github.com/KoljaB/RealtimeVAD/blob/main/SPEC.md)

A voice assistant can't do anything until it knows the user has stopped
talking. Speech recognition, the LLM call and the voice output all wait for
that one decision, and a normal voice activity detector takes a few hundred
milliseconds to make it.

RealtimeVAD makes it sooner. It keeps [Silero VAD](https://github.com/snakers4/silero-vad)
to decide what is speech, and adds a second, faster check: every 10 ms it
compares the audio level with the room's noise. The moment the audio goes
quiet, you get an event, long before Silero's probability has fallen.

- **Input:** 16 kHz mono audio in chunks of any size (float32, int16 or int16 bytes).
- **Output:** `start`, `pause` and `end` events, plus the audio of the running segment at any time.
- **Lead:** speech-off a median 110 ms before Silero's probability drops, and 214 ms before Silero's `VADIterator` reports the end, on 3,238 real turns.
- **Price:** it also fires in short gaps between words, about ten times as often as Silero.
- **Runs on:** one CPU thread, far faster than realtime. Needs only numpy and onnxruntime; the Silero model is bundled, no torch.
- **Status:** alpha (0.0.4). The API may still change.

## Live demo

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d01900dd-9601-4f3d-8c88-db55e8bc83a1

The video uses a synthetic voice and shows a median lead of 92 ms. The 110 ms above is the median on real voice-assistant turns.

[demo/](https://github.com/KoljaB/RealtimeVAD/blob/main/demo/README.md) runs this page on your own microphone. It shows, turn by turn, how much sooner
RealtimeVAD knew that you stopped than Silero alone, on the same audio.

## Quick start

```bash
pip install realtimevad
```

```python
from RealtimeVAD import VAD

vad = VAD()
for chunk in microphone_chunks():
    for event in vad.feed(chunk):
        if event.kind == "start":
            stream_to_asr(vad.audio())       # includes the audio just before speech began
        elif event.kind == "pause":
            speculate(vad.audio())           # the speaker may be done; this isn't the end yet
        elif event.kind == "end":
            finalize(event.segment.audio)
```

candidates.readme_excerpt: # Firecrawl MCP Server A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that brings [Firecrawl](https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl), the context API for AI agents, to MCP-compatible clients: search, scrape, and interact with the live web and get back clean Markdown or structured data. > Big thanks to [@vrknetha](https://github.com/vrknetha), [@knacklabs](https://www.knacklabs.ai) for the initial implementation! ## Features - Search the web, optionally with full page content for each result - Search indexes for developer sources (GitHub issues, merged pull requests, READMEs, and docs), US government sources, and scientific papers (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv, arXiv) - Scrape any URL into clean Markdown - Parse PDFs and documents - Crawl a site for content from many pages, or map it to discover its URLs - Interact with pages in a real browser: click, type, fill forms, and navigate dynamic pages - Run Agent jobs for multi-source research that returns structured data - Monitor pages and get notified when their content changes - Check current and historical Firecrawl credit usage - Automatic retries and rate limiting - Cloud and self-hosted support - SSE support > Play around with [our MCP Server on MCP.so's playground](https://mcp.so/playground?server=firecrawl-mcp-server) or on [Klavis AI](https://www.klavis.ai/mcp-servers). ## When to Use This Server - Use `firecrawl_scrape` when you have a known URL and want its content as markdown, then extract the requested fields yourself. - Use `firecrawl_map` when you need to discover URLs on a site without fetching their content. - Use `firecrawl_crawl` when you need content from many pages under a site; set `limit`, `includePaths`/`excludePaths`, or `maxDiscoveryDepth` to bound it. - Use `firecrawl_search` when you're starting from a query rather than a URL and want ranked web results. Results carry excerpts; fetch full pages with `firecrawl_scrape` on the URLs you need. `scrapeOptions` fetches every result's page in the same call and bills each as a scrape, so keep it for the full text of a few results (the search-only endpoint never fetches content). - Use `firecrawl_interact` when a page needs a click, type, or navigate action before you can read it: pass a `url` for a fresh page or a `scrapeId` to continue on one you already scraped. - Use t

# STE80 Humanizer

[![skills.sh installs](https://skills.sh/b/Dodaios/ste80-humanizer)](https://skills.sh/Dodaios/ste80-humanizer) [![validate](https://github.com/Dodaios/ste80-humanizer/actions/workflows/validate.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Dodaios/ste80-humanizer/actions/workflows/validate.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

STE80 Humanizer makes AI-written text read like a careful person wrote it, without changing what it says. It combines two methods:

1. **The humanizer method.** Remove the 26 tells from Wikipedia's [Signs of AI writing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Signs_of_AI_writing), in the catalog of [blader/humanizer](https://github.com/blader/humanizer).
2. **Karpathy's STE80 method.** Rebuild the sentences "80% of the way to ASD-STE100", the controlled English of aircraft maintenance manuals.

**Before:**
> Great question! Kubernetes liveness probes are a powerful mechanism that enables the kubelet to determine whether a container is healthy — and it's not just a health check, it's your first line of defense. When a probe fails, the container will be automatically restarted by the kubelet, ensuring that your application remains available. However, it's important to note that misconfigured probes could potentially cause cascading restarts, so parameters like `initialDelaySeconds` and `failureThreshold` should be carefully tuned.
>
> Get this right, and your cluster heals itself.

**After:**
> A liveness probe tells the kubelet if a container is healthy. If the probe fails, the kubelet restarts the container. This keeps the application available.
>
> A bad probe can also cause many restarts. For example, a timeout that is too short makes healthy containers fail the probe. To prevent this, set `initialDelaySeconds` and `failureThreshold` to values that fit your application.

The goal is text that people read easily. Getting past AI detectors is not a goal.

Most humanizers only remove phrases. The text loses "Great question!" and "seamless", but it keeps long sentences that carry three ideas, hide the actor and stack hedges. It still reads like AI. You can see it in the worked example in [SKILL.md](SKILL.md):

These ones are packaged so AI agents follow them consistently across every phase of development. ![Addy's Agent Skills](https://addyosmani.com/assets/images/addys-agent-skills.jpg) ``` DEFINE PLAN BUILD VERIFY REVIEW SHIP ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ │ Idea │ ───▶ │ Spec │ ───▶ │ Code │ ───▶ │ Test │ ───▶ │ QA │ ───▶ │ Go │ │Refine│ │ PRD │ │ Impl │ │Debug │ │ Gate │ │ Live │ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ /spec /plan /build /test /review /ship ``` --- ## Commands 9 slash commands that map to the development lifecycle. Each one activates the right skills automatically. | What you're doing | Command | Key principle | |-------------------|---------|---------------| | Define what to build | `/spec` | Spec before code | | Plan how to build it | `/plan` | Small, atomic tasks | | Build incrementally | `/build` | One slice at a time | | Prove it works | `/test` | Tests are proof | | Set the quality bar | `/constraints` | Decide it once, enforce it everywhere | | Review before merge | `/review` | Improve code health | | Audit web performance | `/webperf` | Measure before you optimize | | Simplify the code | `/code-simplify` | Clarity over cleverness | | Ship to production | `/ship` | Faster is safer | In Claude Code these install as plugin commands. It removes the human stepping *between* tasks, not the verification: every task is still test-driven and committed individually, and it pauses on failures or risky steps.
